scenes.purpose: Introduce the concept of gravity and the lesson topic.
scenes.teacher_script: Hello, young scientists! Have you ever wondered why things fall down and not up? Today, we're going to explore the fascinating force that keeps our feet on the ground and planets in orbit: gravity.

content.image_prompt: A stylized illustration of the Earth with an apple falling towards it, a question mark floating above, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.purpose: Define gravity as a fundamental force of attraction.
scenes.teacher_script: Gravity is an invisible force that pulls any two objects with mass towards each other. The more mass an object has, the stronger its gravitational pull. Think of it as a cosmic hug!

content.image_prompt: Two spherical objects of different sizes in space, with subtle curved lines or arrows indicating an attractive force pulling them towards each other, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.purpose: Explain how mass affects the strength of gravity.
scenes.teacher_script: The strength of gravity depends on two main things: the mass of the objects and the distance between them. Let's see how mass plays a role.

content.image_prompt: Two small, equal-sized celestial bodies in space, with very faint, short arrows showing a weak gravitational pull between them, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

Two large, equal-sized celestial bodies in space, with prominent, longer arrows showing a strong gravitational pull between them, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.purpose: Explain how distance affects the strength of gravity.
scenes.teacher_script: Now, let's look at distance. The closer two objects are, the stronger the gravitational force between them. As they move farther apart, the pull becomes weaker.

content.image_prompt: Two large, equal-sized celestial bodies very close to each other in space, with strong, short arrows showing a powerful gravitational pull between them, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

Two large, equal-sized celestial bodies far apart from each other in space, with faint, long arrows showing a weak gravitational pull between them, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.teacher_script: On Earth, gravity is what pulls everything towards its center. This is why when you jump, you come back down, and why an apple falls from a tree to the ground.

content.image_prompt: A simplified illustration of the Earth with a person standing on its surface, showing an arrow pointing from the person towards the center of the Earth, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

An apple falling from a tree branch towards the ground on Earth, with a downward arrow indicating the direction of fall, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.purpose: Explain gravity's role in the solar system.
scenes.teacher_script: Gravity isn't just on Earth; it's everywhere in space! It's the force that keeps planets orbiting the Sun and moons orbiting planets, creating the beautiful dance of our solar system.

content.image_prompt: A simplified illustration of the Sun at the center with several planets orbiting it in elliptical paths, showing gravitational pull lines from the Sun to the planets, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

A simplified illustration of Earth with its Moon orbiting around it, showing gravitational pull lines between Earth and the Moon, clean educational illustration style, no text, no labels, no annotations, no watermarks, no overlays

scenes.purpose: Summarize the key concepts of gravity.
scenes.teacher_script: So, gravity is a universal force of attraction. It depends on the mass of objects and the distance between them. It's what keeps us grounded and the cosmos in motion!

left_bullets: Keeps us on Earth and planets in orbit
